subject.title: backup create stalls on large installations (4GB+ .openclaw dir)

question: What restore-safe native behavior should `openclaw backup create` support for large state directories: smart/custom exclusions, a smaller completion/error fix, or documented current-scope limits with plugin workarounds?
rationale: Choosing default exclusions, protected backup contents, and progress/size policy affects restore completeness and sensitive local state, and the active linked PR changes user-facing backup policy rather than only fixing a mechanical failure.

options.title: Review linked PR as canonical
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement after resolving conflicts, proof, protected-path semantics, and external-asset behavior.

options.title: Ship reliability first
options.body: Prioritize making the existing full backup complete or fail clearly with progress and size guidance, while deferring custom exclusions to the broader backup-scope tracker.

options.title: Defer core scope expansion
options.body: Document current core backup limits and point optional backup strategies to ClawHub only if maintainers intentionally keep native exclusions outside core for now.

recommendation.title: Review linked PR as canonical
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement after resolving conflicts, proof, protected-path semantics, and external-asset behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to both the original backup CLI behavior and the current infra extraction, making them the strongest routing candidate for the core backup contract decision.
